hypothesis: Rivet's next differentiator is Trust Infrastructure: per-tool-call undo + context visibility, not more features

fragments.text: User trust = visibility + rollback-ability. Two legs of the same chair.
Checkpoint is per-run (git HEAD hash), not per-tool-call. DAW time-travel needs new storage layer.
Only 3 of 15+ 'dormant' features are truly wire-and-go (autoReasoning, lspEnabled, tool registration)
Claude Code consumes 3-4x more tokens than Codex per equivalent task. DeepSeek cache = 4x cost advantage.
No terminal coding agent lets users SEE context management. ACF is invisible to users without /context.
DAW scoped-undo: each edit surface maintains independent undo/redo stack. Focus switch routes to correct history.
lazygit priority-based responsive hiding: UI elements have priority groups, low-priority hides first when space shrinks.
BAML partial object streaming: stream semantic-valid partial objects, not characters. UI can start processing before generation completes.

extinctions.reason: Goal loop without per-call undo is a ticking bomb. Causal chain broken.

survivors.advantage: Solves pain point #2, prerequisite for V4
Makes ACF investment visible, solves pain point #1

finalPlan: V1 (half day) → V2+V3 parallel (3 days) = Wave 5 Trust Infrastructure
